n.sample_role: nondieting participants; low versus high subjective SES on food IAT
n.exclusions: 1008 excluded because no IAT score could be obtained; 379 additional exclusions for dieting/food regulation; report contains one-person discrepancy in intermediate total.
n.quote: Replication results: In the replication experiment, the mean implicit preference for calorie- dense food in the low SES condition was 0.080 (sd = 0.621; n = 482), compared to 0.113 (sd = 0.587; n = 443 in the high SES condition. The difference of 0.033 (se = 0.040) was tested using an independent-samples t-test assuming equal variances (t(923) = 0.827, p = 0.408; n = 925). As a result, we cannot reject the null hypothesis of equal implicit preference for calorie-dense foods in the high SES condition compared to the low SES condition. Note that the difference in the replication experiment is in the opposite direction of the difference in the original article. The standardized effect size (Cohen’s d) is d = –0.054 (95% CI [–0.183, 0.075]).
